KLOW.subtitle: The KLOW Blend
KLOW.summary: KLOW is a combination of four peptides — GHK-Cu, KPV, BPC-157, and TB-500 — currently studied across several research areas involving tissue, immune, and cellular signaling pathways.

ingredients.name: GHK-Cu
ingredients.label: Copper Peptide
ingredients.researchArea: Collagen synthesis signaling, tissue remodeling, antioxidant activity, and angiogenesis pathway research.

ingredients.name: KPV
ingredients.label: Tripeptide
ingredients.researchArea: Inflammatory signaling pathways and immune modulation research, particularly in gastrointestinal and skin tissue contexts.

ingredients.name: BPC-157
ingredients.label: Body Protection Compound
ingredients.researchArea: Musculoskeletal tissue signaling, gastrointestinal tract research, nerve signaling, and angiogenesis pathway research.

ingredients.name: TB-500
ingredients.label: Thymosin Beta-4 Fragment
ingredients.researchArea: Cell migration signaling, tissue repair pathways, and flexibility-related research.

citations.label: Pickart & Margolina (2018) — GHK-Cu regenerative signaling review
Sikiric et al. (2016) — BPC-157 tissue signaling review

KLOW.consultationNote: Dosing, scheduling, and reconstitution information is reviewed during a consultation.

GLP-3 (retatrutide).subtitle: Triple GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon Receptor Agonist
GLP-3 (retatrutide).summary: Retatrutide is an investigational triagonist peptide studied for simultaneous activity at GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors. It is one of the most closely watched compounds in current metabolic research, with Phase 2 trial results published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2023.

researchAreas.detail: Studies investigate how simultaneous agonism at GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors may influence metabolic signaling cascades differently than single or dual receptor agents. Retatrutide is considered a 'triagonist' in this research context.

links.label: Jastreboff et al. 2023 — NEJM Phase 2 Trial

researchAreas.detail: Phase 2 research (the TRIUMPH-4 trial, NCT05071326) examined effects on body weight and cardiometabolic markers in adult populations over 48 weeks. Findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2023.

links.label: TRIUMPH-4 — ClinicalTrials NCT05071326
Jastreboff et al. 2023 — NEJM

researchAreas.detail: Researchers investigate retatrutide's role in hypothalamic appetite-signaling pathways and its interactions with the incretin hormone system — the GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon axis — that regulate energy balance and glucose homeostasis.
Ongoing trials examine changes in lipid profiles, liver fat, blood pressure, and other cardiometabolic markers in the context of triagonist signaling pathway research.

links.label: ClinicalTrials NCT05071326

citations.label: Jastreboff et al. (2023) — Retatrutide Phase 2 (NEJM)
TRIUMPH-4 — ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05071326

GLP-3 (retatrutide).researchNote: Investigational compound; not FDA-approved. Research is ongoing in Phase 3 trials.

Oxytocin.subtitle: Peptide Hormone & Neurotransmitter
Oxytocin.summary: Oxytocin is a naturally occurring neuropeptide and hormone produced in the hypothalamus and released by the pituitary gland. It is studied for its roles across several signaling pathways including stress modulation, social behavior, mood, metabolism, sexual function, and pain research.

researchAreas.detail: Researchers study oxytocin's interaction with the amygdala and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, investigating its role in cortisol regulation and stress-response modulation pathways.

links.label: Meyer-Lindenberg et al. 2011 — Oxytocin and social behavior (Nature Reviews)

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine its influence on social recognition, trust signaling, and affiliative behavior research in both animal models and human subjects.

links.label: Meyer-Lindenberg et al. 2011 — Oxytocin and social behavior

researchAreas.detail: Research investigates oxytocin's interaction with serotonin and dopamine pathways and its role in mood-related signaling research.

links.label: Guastella & MacLeod 2012 — Oxytocin and anxiety pathways

researchAreas.detail: Studies explore its role in energy balance, appetite-regulating neural pathways, and metabolic signaling research.
Research examines its role in reproductive behavior, arousal-related pathways, and intimacy-related neuroendocrine signaling.

links.label: Meyer-Lindenberg et al. 2011 — Oxytocin neuroendocrine signaling

researchAreas.detail: Researchers study oxytocin's interaction with spinal pain-modulation pathways and opioid receptor signaling in the context of pain research.

citations.label: Meyer-Lindenberg et al. (2011) — Oxytocin and social behavior (Nature Reviews)
Guastella & MacLeod (2012) — Oxytocin and social-anxiety pathways

Oxytocin.researchNote: Naturally occurring hormone; investigational for many of the uses described. Not medical advice.

PT-141.subtitle: Melanocortin Receptor Research Peptide
PT-141.summary: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is a synthetic melanocortin receptor agonist studied for its activity at MC3 and MC4 receptors in the central nervous system. A pharmaceutical version (Vyleesi) received FDA approval for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women in 2019.

researchAreas.detail: Research focuses on PT-141's activity at MC3 and MC4 receptors and its downstream effects on dopamine and norepinephrine signaling pathways in the central nervous system.

links.label: FDA — Vyleesi (bremelanotide) prescribing information

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine its role in libido-related neural pathways, sexual arousal signaling, and desire-related CNS activity in both men and women. Phase 3 trials leading to Vyleesi's FDA approval enrolled over 1,200 women.

links.label: Simon et al. 2014 — Bremelanotide Phase 3 results
FDA — Vyleesi prescribing information (2019)

researchAreas.detail: Researchers investigate its influence on dopaminergic pathways involved in mood, motivation, and reward-system signaling research.

links.label: Simon et al. 2014 — Bremelanotide Phase 3 results

researchAreas.detail: Studies explore its role in central nervous system activation signaling, alertness pathways, and energy-related neurological research.

citations.label: FDA — Vyleesi (bremelanotide) prescribing information (2019)
Simon et al. (2014) — Bremelanotide Phase 3 trial results

PT-141.researchNote: Vyleesi (bremelanotide) is FDA-approved for HSDD in premenopausal women. PT-141 as a research peptide is investigational for other uses. Not medical advice.

Epithalon.subtitle: Telomerase-Activating Tetrapeptide
Epithalon.summary: Epithalon (Epitalon) is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) developed by Dr. Vladimir Khavinson at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. It is studied for its potential influence on telomerase activity and cellular aging research pathways.

researchAreas.detail: Studies by Khavinson et al. investigated Epithalon's ability to activate telomerase enzyme in human somatic cells, examining its potential influence on telomere length maintenance in the context of cellular aging research.

links.label: Khavinson et al. 2003 — Epithalon and telomerase activation

researchAreas.detail: Research explores Epithalon's relationship to melatonin production and pineal gland function in aging subjects, examining circadian signaling pathway changes associated with the aging pineal gland.
Preclinical studies examine Epithalon's effects on cellular senescence markers, oxidative stress-related signaling, and longevity-associated gene expression pathway research.
Research has investigated Epithalon's effects on hypothalamic-pituitary axis signaling and melatonin/cortisol rhythm research in aging study populations.

citations.label: Khavinson et al. (2003) — Epithalon and telomerase activation in human cells
Anisimov et al. (2003) — Epithalamin/Epitalon in longevity pathway research

Epithalon.researchNote: Investigational compound in cellular aging research; most published studies are preclinical or from a small number of research groups.

Semax.subtitle: ACTH Fragment Analog Neuropeptide
Semax.summary: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of the ACTH(4–10) fragment, developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences. It is studied for its activity in cognitive signaling, BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor) expression, and neuroprotective pathway research. It is registered as a pharmaceutical in Russia.

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine Semax's influence on attention, working memory-related neural pathways, and nootropic signaling research. It is registered in Russia for applications including ischemic stroke recovery and cognitive signaling research.

Research has reported Semax's influence on BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor), VEGF, and NGF expression in brain tissue, with implications for neuroplasticity and neuroprotective pathway research.

links.label: Dolotov et al. 2006 — Semax and BDNF expression in rat brain

researchAreas.detail: Preclinical studies have investigated Semax in models of ischemia and oxidative neurological stress, examining its potential effects on neuroprotective cellular signaling pathways.
Research explores Semax's interactions with dopaminergic and serotonergic signaling systems and their relevance to mood and cognitive performance pathway research.

citations.label: Dolotov et al. (2006) — Semax and BDNF expression in rat brain
Lebedeva et al. (2008) — Semax in cognitive pathway investigations

Semax.researchNote: Registered pharmaceutical in Russia; investigational in most other regions. Cognitive signaling research compound.

Selank.subtitle: Tuftsin Analog Neuropeptide
Selank.summary: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of tuftsin (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg), developed by the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences. It is studied for its activity in stress-response, anxiety-related signaling, and immune modulation pathways, and is registered as a pharmaceutical in Russia.

researchAreas.detail: Studies investigate Selank's effects on anxiety-related neural signaling pathways, including its interactions with GABA-A receptor modulation research and stress-hormone signaling in both animal models and human subjects.

links.label: Semenova et al. 2010 — Selank in anxiety pathway research

researchAreas.detail: Research has reported Selank's influence on BDNF expression and the balance between BDNF and other neurotrophic factors involved in mood-regulation and cognitive pathway research.

links.label: Zozulya et al. 2001 — Selank and BDNF signaling

researchAreas.detail: As a tuftsin analog, Selank is studied for interactions between immune signaling (cytokine modulation) and central nervous system pathway research, examining psychoneuroimmunology connections.

Preclinical and clinical studies investigate Selank's influence on learning, memory consolidation pathways, and cognitive signaling research, related to its effects on enkephalin catabolism and neurotransmitter systems.

citations.label: Semenova et al. (2010) — Selank in anxiety pathway research
Zozulya et al. (2001) — Selank enkephalin and BDNF signaling

Selank.researchNote: Registered pharmaceutical in Russia; investigational in most other regions. Stress-response pathway research compound.

Ipamorelin + CJC-1295.subtitle: Growth Hormone Secretagogue Combination
Ipamorelin + CJC-1295.summary: This combination pairs Ipamorelin, a selective GHRP (growth hormone releasing peptide), with CJC-1295, a GHRH (growth hormone releasing hormone) analog. Research studies how pairing a pituitary GHSR agonist with a hypothalamic GHRH analog affects growth hormone axis signaling.

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine how Ipamorelin acts on GHSR (growth hormone secretagogue receptor) while CJC-1295 binds GHRH receptors, and research investigates whether this combination produces additive effects on GH pulse amplitude via two separate signaling pathways.

links.label: Raun et al. 1998 — Ipamorelin pharmacology
Teichman et al. 2006 — CJC-1295 Phase 1/2

researchAreas.detail: Research explores how sustained GH elevation through combined GHRH/GHRP signaling may affect downstream IGF-1 signaling pathways and their relationship to cellular anabolism pathway research.
Phase 1/2 clinical studies with CJC-1295 investigated changes in lean tissue and fat mass markers. Research continues on the combined signaling effects on metabolic and body composition pathways.
Research investigates the relationship between GH secretagogue signaling and nocturnal growth hormone pulse research, which naturally peaks during slow-wave sleep phases.

citations.label: Raun et al. (1998) — Ipamorelin pharmacology and GH selectivity
Teichman et al. (2006) — CJC-1295 Phase 1/2 pharmacokinetics

Ipamorelin + CJC-1295.researchNote: Growth hormone axis research; both are investigational compounds.

Ipamorelin.subtitle: Selective Growth Hormone Secretagogue
Ipamorelin.summary: Ipamorelin is a selective, third-generation pentapeptide growth hormone releasing peptide (GHRP) studied for its activity at GHSR (growth hormone secretagogue receptor) signaling pathways. It is distinguished in research for its high GH-release selectivity with minimal effect on cortisol or prolactin.

researchAreas.detail: Research focuses on Ipamorelin's binding selectivity at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR-1a) and its downstream signaling cascade leading to pituitary GH release without significant crosstalk to cortisol or prolactin pathways.
Studies examine how Ipamorelin influences the amplitude and frequency of GH secretion pulses and its relationship to downstream IGF-1 production signaling in liver and peripheral tissues.
Research investigates Ipamorelin's influence on fat oxidation signaling, lean tissue preservation pathways, and metabolic rate-related cellular processes.

citations.label: Raun et al. (1998) — Ipamorelin: a new growth hormone releasing peptide

Ipamorelin.researchNote: Growth hormone secretagogue research; investigational compound.

CJC-1295.subtitle: Long-Acting GHRH Analog
CJC-1295.summary: CJC-1295 is a synthetic analog of GHRH (growth hormone releasing hormone) modified to extend its plasma half-life through albumin binding. It is studied for its role in growth hormone signaling, extended half-life pharmacokinetics, and downstream cellular pathway research.

researchAreas.detail: Research examines CJC-1295's binding to GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotrophs and its stimulation of GH release, comparing its signaling profile to native GHRH with its extended half-life pharmacokinetics.
Phase 1/2 clinical studies investigated sustained elevations in IGF-1 following CJC-1295 administration, with research examining downstream anabolic signaling pathway effects.

The DAC (drug affinity complex) technology in CJC-1295 enables albumin binding that extends half-life to several days. Research investigates this pharmacokinetic modification and its implications for GH axis signaling duration.

citations.label: Teichman et al. (2006) — CJC-1295 Phase 1/2 clinical pharmacokinetics

MOTS-c.subtitle: Mitochondria-Derived Peptide
MOTS-c.summary: MOTS-c is a 16-amino acid peptide encoded within the mitochondrial genome (12S rRNA gene). It is one of a class of mitochondria-derived peptides (MDPs) recognized for its signaling roles that extend well beyond the mitochondria, traveling to the cytosol, plasma, and nucleus.

researchAreas.detail: Research focuses on MOTS-c's activation of AMPK signaling pathways involved in glucose uptake, lipid metabolism, and overall metabolic regulation in skeletal muscle tissue and other organs.

links.label: Lee et al. 2015 — MOTS-c discovery (Cell Metabolism)

researchAreas.detail: Preclinical studies have investigated MOTS-c's potential influence on insulin receptor signaling and glucose transporter (GLUT4) pathway activity in muscle and adipose tissue.

links.label: Lee et al. 2015 — MOTS-c discovery (Cell Metabolism)

researchAreas.detail: Research explores how MOTS-c travels from mitochondria to the nucleus to regulate gene expression involved in nuclear AMPK signaling and metabolic stress response pathways — a novel form of retrograde mitochondrial signaling.

links.label: Kim et al. 2018 — MOTS-c nuclear AMPK signaling

researchAreas.detail: Studies have noted that circulating MOTS-c levels decline with age and increase with exercise. Research investigates its relationship to age-related metabolic changes and longevity-associated signaling pathway research.

citations.label: Lee et al. (2015) — MOTS-c: A mitochondrial-derived peptide (Cell Metabolism)
Kim et al. (2018) — MOTS-c nuclear AMPK signaling and stress response

MOTS-c.researchNote: Mitochondria-derived peptide; metabolic signaling research. Investigational compound.

SS-31.subtitle: Cardiolipin-Targeting Mitochondrial Tetrapeptide
SS-31.summary: SS-31 (elamipretide) is a synthetic tetrapeptide that selectively concentrates in the inner mitochondrial membrane, where it interacts with cardiolipin. It is studied for its role in mitochondrial membrane function, cellular energy pathway research, and mitochondrial integrity signaling.

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine SS-31's selective interaction with cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane, researching how this affects electron transport chain efficiency and overall mitochondrial structural integrity signaling.

links.label: Birk et al. 2013 — SS-31 and cardiolipin (Circulation Research)

researchAreas.detail: Research investigates how SS-31's cardiolipin interaction influences ATP synthase activity, oxidative phosphorylation pathways, and overall cellular bioenergetics in high-energy-demand tissues.

Studies explore SS-31's potential to reduce mitochondrial ROS (reactive oxygen species) production and its effects on cellular oxidative stress signaling pathways in preclinical aging and disease models.

Elamipretide has been investigated in clinical studies for mitochondria-related cardiac conditions and renal function signaling. Research examines its effects in ischemia-reperfusion and heart failure pathway contexts.

links.label: Daubert et al. 2017 — Elamipretide Phase 2 heart failure trial

citations.label: Birk et al. (2013) — SS-31 and cardiolipin interactions (Circulation Research)
Daubert et al. (2017) — Elamipretide Phase 2 heart failure trial

SS-31.researchNote: Mitochondrial function research; investigational compound with ongoing clinical trials.

Kisspeptin.subtitle: Hypothalamic GnRH Regulator
Kisspeptin.summary: Kisspeptin is a naturally occurring neuropeptide encoded by the KISS1 gene. It is recognized as the central upstream regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, providing the primary signal for GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) release. Its discovery transformed understanding of reproductive hormone signaling.

researchAreas.detail: Research demonstrates that kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus (KNDy neurons) provide the primary upstream signal that drives GnRH pulsatility from the hypothalamus, making kisspeptin the 'master regulator' of the reproductive hormone axis.

links.label: Oakley et al. 2009 — Kisspeptin signaling in the HPG axis

researchAreas.detail: Clinical studies show that kisspeptin administration reliably stimulates LH (luteinizing hormone) and FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) release in humans, with research exploring its role in both male and female hormonal signaling contexts.

links.label: Dhillo et al. 2005 — Kisspeptin-54 stimulates LH/FSH in humans

researchAreas.detail: Research explores kisspeptin's relevance to puberty onset signaling, fertility-related pathways, hypothalamic amenorrhea investigation, and its role in linking metabolic status to reproductive hormone signaling.

Studies also investigate kisspeptin's potential interactions with mood pathways and sexual behavior neural circuits, with clinical research at Imperial College London examining psychosexual signaling effects.

citations.label: Dhillo et al. (2005) — Kisspeptin-54 stimulates LH and FSH in humans
Oakley et al. (2009) — Kisspeptin signaling in the HPG axis

Kisspeptin.researchNote: Reproductive hormone signaling research; investigational for clinical applications.

TA1.subtitle: Thymic Immunomodulatory Peptide
TA1.summary: Thymosin Alpha-1 (TA1) is a 28-amino acid acetylated peptide derived from prothymosin alpha, originally isolated from thymic tissue. It is one of the most studied immunomodulatory peptides, with pharmaceutical approvals in over 35 countries (marketed as Zadaxin) for specific immune-related applications.

researchAreas.detail: Research demonstrates TA1's activity in dendritic cell maturation and T-cell signaling pathways, particularly in stimulating T-helper cell differentiation, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte activation, and regulatory T-cell signaling.

links.label: Ancell & Phipps 2001 — Thymosin Alpha-1 mechanisms review

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine how TA1 bridges innate and adaptive immune signaling pathways, including its effects on toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling, STAT1/3 pathway activation, and natural killer (NK) cell activity research.
Research investigates TA1's influence on cytokine production profiles including IL-2, IL-12, IFN-γ, and TNF-α signaling pathways in immune regulation and anti-inflammatory research contexts.

TA1 (Zadaxin) has been investigated in clinical settings across multiple countries for hepatitis B and hepatitis C treatment adjunct protocols. It is approved in some countries for these applications and as an adjuvant for influenza vaccination in elderly populations.

links.label: Garaci 2007 — Thymosin Alpha-1 clinical review

citations.label: Ancell & Phipps (2001) — Thymosin Alpha-1 immunological mechanisms review
Garaci (2007) — Thymosin Alpha-1 clinical review

TA1.researchNote: Approved in some countries (as Zadaxin) for hepatitis B/C adjunct therapy; investigational in others including the United States.

NAD+.subtitle: Cellular Metabolism Coenzyme
NAD+.summary: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a coenzyme present in all living cells and central to hundreds of enzymatic reactions. Research interest has surged due to its observed decline with aging and its role in longevity-associated signaling pathways. NAD+ precursors such as NMN (nicotinamide mononucleotide) and NR (nicotinamide riboside) are actively studied.

researchAreas.detail: NAD+ is an essential cofactor in the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Research investigates how NAD+ availability influences mitochondrial electron transport chain efficiency and cellular ATP production in aging and disease contexts.

Sirtuins (SIRT1–7) are NAD+-dependent deacetylases linked to aging, inflammation, and metabolic stress. Research explores how NAD+ precursors (NMN, NR) may support sirtuin signaling activity and downstream longevity-associated pathway research.

links.label: Gomes et al. 2013 — NAD+ and mitochondrial homeostasis (Cell)

researchAreas.detail: PARP enzymes consume NAD+ during DNA repair processes. Research examines the interplay between PARP activity, NAD+ availability, and genomic maintenance signaling — and whether NAD+ supplementation strategies affect DNA repair pathway capacity.

links.label: Rajman et al. 2018 — NAD-boosting molecules review (Cell Metabolism)

researchAreas.detail: Studies investigate NAD+ oscillations in the context of circadian rhythm signaling and their relationship to CLOCK gene expression, SIRT1 activity cycles, and metabolic clock pathway research.
Research examines NAD+'s role in neuronal energy supply, SIRT3 mitochondrial signaling in neurons, and potential neuroprotective pathway investigations in age-related neurological research.

links.label: Yoshino et al. 2018 — NMN restores NAD+ in aging (Cell Metabolism)

citations.label: Gomes et al. (2013) — NAD+ and mitochondrial homeostasis (Cell)
Yoshino et al. (2018) — NMN supplementation restores NAD+ in aging mice (Cell Metabolism)
Rajman et al. (2018) — Therapeutic potential of NAD-boosting molecules (Cell Metabolism)

NAD+.researchNote: Cellular metabolism and longevity research. NMN and NR are dietary supplement forms; IV/injectable NAD+ is investigational in clinical settings.

hCG.subtitle: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin
hCG.summary: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone naturally produced during pregnancy by syncytiotrophoblast cells of the placenta. Structurally related to LH (luteinizing hormone), FSH, and TSH, it shares the LH/CG receptor and is studied across reproductive endocrinology and hormonal signaling research.

researchAreas.detail: hCG shares the LH/hCG receptor (LHCGR) with endogenous LH. Research investigates its signaling effects on Leydig cell testosterone production in males and corpus luteum maintenance signaling in females via the same receptor pathway.

hCG is extensively studied and used in reproductive medicine for triggering final oocyte maturation in assisted reproduction protocols and for supporting corpus luteum progesterone production. Its signaling mechanisms in fertility research are well-documented.

links.label: Huhtaniemi 2005 — hCG in reproductive physiology

researchAreas.detail: In men, research investigates hCG's role in supporting testicular function and intratesticular testosterone production, particularly in the context of hormonal optimization and fertility preservation research during testosterone therapy.

links.label: Bassil et al. 2009 — hCG and male reproductive signaling

researchAreas.detail: Studies examine hCG's downstream signaling effects within the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis and its differences from endogenous LH pulsatility in terms of receptor signaling kinetics and downstream pathway activation.

citations.label: Huhtaniemi (2005) — hCG in reproductive physiology review
Bassil et al. (2009) — hCG and male reproductive signaling research

hCG.researchNote: FDA-approved for specific reproductive medicine indications; investigational for other applications described. Discuss with a licensed clinician.

DSIP.summary: Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide (DSIP) is an investigational neuropeptide studied for its potential role in sleep-regulating signaling pathways and circadian rhythm-related research.
DSIP.researchNote: Investigational sleep signaling research; limited clinical data.

Melatonin.summary: Melatonin is a naturally occurring hormone produced by the pineal gland. It is studied for its role in circadian rhythm regulation, photoperiodic signaling, and antioxidant activity research.
Melatonin.researchNote: Circadian rhythm signaling; widely studied. Available OTC in the United States.

Pinealon.summary: Pinealon is an experimental tripeptide studied in preclinical research for its potential neuroprotective signaling properties and its possible interactions with pineal gland function.
Pinealon.researchNote: Experimental neuropeptide research; limited human data.

ARA-290.summary: ARA-290 (cibinetide) is an erythropoietin-derived peptide studied for its activity at the innate repair receptor (IRR). Research explores its role in inflammatory and nerve signaling pathway modulation.
ARA-290.researchNote: Inflammatory and nerve signaling research; investigational compound.

Bromelain.summary: Bromelain is a proteolytic enzyme complex derived from pineapple. It is studied for its activity in inflammatory pathway research, protein digestion, and immune signaling investigations.
Bromelain.researchNote: Dietary enzyme supplement; ongoing research into anti-inflammatory signaling properties.

Omega-3.summary: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) are essential polyunsaturated fats studied for their roles in inflammatory signaling, cardiovascular pathway research, and neurological function investigations.
Omega-3.researchNote: Essential fatty acid supplement; widely researched.

Vitamin C.summary: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is an essential water-soluble nutrient studied for its role in antioxidant activity, collagen synthesis pathways, and immune signaling research.

Selenium.summary: Selenium is an essential trace mineral incorporated into selenoproteins. It is studied for its role in antioxidant enzyme activity, thyroid hormone signaling, and immune function pathway research.

Magnesium.summary: Magnesium is an essential mineral that acts as a cofactor in over 300 enzymatic reactions. It is studied for its role in muscle and nerve signaling, energy metabolism, and DNA synthesis pathway research.
